long_biography.plain_text:
Stengos graduated from the National Technical University of Athens and led public works in Achaia before establishing Pelops in Patras in 1965. The company moved from regional roads into hydraulic, harbour, building and electromechanical projects, gained national reach, adopted the Technical Olympic name and listed in Athens. His related venture Mochlos added major contracting capacity and ready-mix concrete.

Growth came through American residential builders, the Porto Carras complex, marina operations and renewable energy. The disposal of the resort assets released capital for a different portfolio: containership interests, property development in several countries, Samos marina management and energy projects. Shipping subsequently became the group's largest reported operating segment. Konstantinos still heads the board, while Georgios serves as chief executive and Marianna as an executive director—roles that keep founder ownership distinct from day-to-day succession.
